marks.title: Sand and Silence
marks.description: You stood in the Ring while law was made, and heard the crowd stop breathing.

marks.title: A Champion's Word
marks.description: Cassian Vale told you a thing he had told no one, and unlocked a door to prove it.

marks.title: Dated Before the Blood
marks.description: The seal came open in the lantern light, and the date on it came before the fight it decided.

marks.title: Nothing Leaves Corvane Unread
marks.description: You left the city carrying a judgement, and no clerk ever turned the page.

marks.title: Seven Names on the Road
marks.description: Seven places have stopped being rumour to you.

marks.title: A House Remembers You
marks.description: You named a seal aloud in front of the people it ruined, and the hand behind it heard.

marks.title: Paid in Full
marks.description: The fix stood, the sand drank a champion, and your purse was heavy walking away from it.

marks.title: A Crown Without a Wound
marks.description: Aldermere changed hands and nobody bled for it, except the ones who were owed.

marks.title: A Century Undone
marks.description: Every judgement carved into that wall is now only carving, and the houses have taken up arms over it.

marks.title: Won on the Sand
marks.description: You burned the proof and settled it the old way, honestly, and inherited every rotten thing you were fighting.

standing.title: The Sable Court
standing.description: The houses want the succession quiet. A whisper against you here becomes a warrant somewhere else.

standing.title: The Iron Fane
standing.description: The temple certifies every Verdict. If judgements are known to be bought, a century of its work is void, and it knows that better than you do.

standing.title: Thornhollow
standing.description: Nine years of plaintiffs behind a thorn palisade. They have been waiting for someone to bring them a seal, and they can tell who enjoyed the Ring.

standing.title: The Verdict Ring
standing.description: The Ring is a faction of its own: champions, keepers and the crowd. It rewards those who honour the sand and never forgives smuggling.

endings.title: The Verdict Upheld
endings.cost: The fix stands and you are paid for it. Cassian Vale throws the succession Verdict and dies on the sand.
endings.reign_description: You are rich and you are complicit. The Court owns your calendar and sends for you, and the sending is never a request.

endings.title: The Bloodless Crown
endings.cost: The succession passes with no fight and the Ring is reformed. Thornhollow get nothing, and they know it.
endings.reign_description: The Ring answers to a new charter you helped write. Every house you embarrassed to write it remembers your part exactly.

endings.title: The Broken Ring
endings.cost: A century of Verdicts is void. The land goes back to the people it was taken from, and so does open war between the houses.
endings.reign_description: Aldermere is contested ground. Places change hands while your back is turned, roads close, and what you keep is only what you can hold.

endings.title: The Iron Verdict
endings.cost: The system stands, unbroken and unquestioned, and it is now yours to abuse.
endings.reign_description: You own the Ring. You schedule Verdicts, which means you decide what Aldermere is permitted to argue about next.

ledger.title: The Ledger
ledger.description: Your own record of every Verdict you have stood at. Three of the four roads out of this end with you handing it to someone.

entry_fields.label: Entry
entry_fields.description: Its number in your hand, counted from the first Verdict you ever saw.

entry_fields.label: Dated
entry_fields.description: The day it was settled, as the calendar of Aldermere reckons it.

entry_fields.label: Where
entry_fields.description: The location it was settled in.

entry_fields.label: The matter
entry_fields.description: What was actually being argued over, in one line.

entry_fields.label: Claimants
entry_fields.description: The parties whose quarrel it was, named.

entry_fields.label: On the sand
entry_fields.description: Who fought, and for which claimant.

entry_fields.label: Your part
entry_fields.description: Whether you watched it, fought it, judged it, or had it written against you.

entry_fields.label: Decided
entry_fields.description: What the Ring made law, and who it made poorer.

entry_fields.label: Certified
entry_fields.description: The hand and seal that put the judgement beyond appeal.

entry_fields.label: What you saw
entry_fields.description: Anything you noticed that the carving on the wall does not say. Blank on an honest Verdict; this is the column that makes the Ledger evidence.

entry_fields.label: Since
entry_fields.description: What the world did afterwards, filled in as you learn it.

written_when.condition: The player is present when a Verdict is settled, in the Ring or anywhere a Verdict is held.
written_when.note: Includes the opening Verdict, which is the first entry every Ledger carries.

written_when.condition: The player fights a Verdict themselves and it resolves either way.
The player loses a Verdict and a judgement is written against them, which they then carry where anyone may read it.
After the ending, a Petition brought to the player is judged, fought, refused or sold.
written_when.note: The same entry shape, so the Ledger keeps growing once the authored story is spent.

written_when.condition: An existing entry is amended, never replaced, when the world reveals what a past Verdict actually cost.

handover.description: In three of the four endings the Ledger leaves your hands, and what it says is what those endings are built out of. If you die after the succession Verdict it passes to whoever was standing nearest you, and the story carries on from their side of it.
